title: Migrate apps/architecture-studio from a plain TypeScript/Vite SPA to Next.js (App Router), preserving the read-only Graph IR explorer surface's behavior exactly
objective: Owner-directed: 'Vamos refatorar o architecture studio para usar next e colocar os elementos para testar tudo + ia + o que esta planejado.' Per the approved plan (C:\Users\PICHAU\.claude\plans\mellow-drifting-nova.md, Phase B) and ADR-0016 (Accepted, DEC-054), this task performs the framework migration itself: apps/architecture-studio becomes a Next.js App Router application, reusing the exact Rust->Wasm->Dedicated-Worker->Next.js-client-route pattern already proven by spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs (wasm-pack output copied as a static asset under public/, loaded via a runtime-variable import(/* webpackIgnore: true */ ...) inside the Worker). The existing Graph IR explorer surface's behavior must not change: same read-only canvas, same entity list/inspector/copy actions, same Rust-computed grouped-grid layout via the same layout_graph_json Wasm export. Pure logic/data modules (canvas-composition.ts, canvas-views.ts, presentation.ts, layout-client.ts) move unchanged; only main.ts (becomes a 'use client' React component), style.css (becomes globals.css), layout.worker.ts (Wasm-loading half rewritten to the static-asset pattern), and the app's own build/test tooling (package.json, project.json, tsconfig.json) change. Explicitly out of scope for this task: the VTT generation-test surface and the agent-orchestration surface (separate, later tasks per the plan's Phase C/D).
validations: DONE: node --test test/*.test.mjs -- all 8 pre-existing canvas-composition/presentation tests pass unchanged.

DONE: tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit passes clean (both before and after Next.js's own build-time tsconfig auto-patch: jsx -> react-jsx, allowJs added, .next/dev/types include added -- these are Next's own mandatory/suggested changes, kept as-is).
DONE: next build (Turbopack) succeeds; root route prerenders as static content.

DONE: next dev started at http://127.0.0.1:4511/; curl-verified HTTP 200 with the expected SSR shell markers present (topbar, entity-list, #graph, inspector-content, 'Loading Graph IR v1…'); curl-verified /wasm-pkg/grafting_isekai_wasm.js and /wasm-pkg/grafting_isekai_wasm_bg.wasm are both served with HTTP 200 (16248 and 196014 bytes respectively), confirming the static-asset Wasm-serving pattern from spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs works end to end for the real app.

DONE: docs-generate re-run for architecture-studio; docs/generated/api/ts/architecture-studio.api.md is byte-identical to its pre-migration content (this app has no public package-API surface), so no docs-quality-check review was needed.
DONE: real-browser interactive confirmation performed by the repository owner directly (canvas rendering, click-to-select, Worker+Wasm layout computation) -- confirmed working.
risks: Discovery: next build (Turbopack) does not resolve the pre-existing '.js'-extension-pointing-to-'.ts'-source convention (nor a literal '.ts' extension) that this app's own source files used for cross-imports (presentation.ts imported './layout-client.js' and './canvas-views.ts'); tsc's Bundler moduleResolution and Vite both accepted this, Turbopack does not. Fixed by dropping the extension entirely on these internal specifiers (canvas-composition.ts, presentation.ts, layout.worker.ts, and the new explorer-client.tsx) -- a mechanical specifier-only change, no logic/behavior change. Scope was widened to include canvas-composition.ts and presentation.ts for this reason.

Next.js's default build output (.next/) differs from this repo's DEC-045/GATE-007 dist/<app> distribution convention; this task updates the Nx build target's outputs field to match reality (.next/) rather than forcing a distDir hack Next.js itself discourages, and flags reconciling this with DEC-045's framing as a separate, small owner-facing question -- not resolved here.

This is the first real (non-spike) Next.js usage in the Nx workspace; package versions are pinned to exactly what spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs already proved compatible (next ^16.2.12, typescript ^5.9.3 -- typescript@latest resolves to 7.x, which Next 16.2.12's type-checker rejects, a real issue the spike already hit).
Deploy runtime (Node vs Edge) is not validated by this task, consistent with the spike's own flagged open risk -- this task only targets local dev/build parity, not a production deployment target.

No dependency was added without evaluation: next/react/react-dom versions match what @grafting/ui and @grafting/x6-canvas already use as devDependencies (react/react-dom 19.2.8), avoiding a second React version in the workspace.
